response.evidence: Out of 8 loan applications for 35-44 year-old non-Hispanic Black or African American males, 6 were approved (a 75% approval rate). The 2 denied applications had identifiable financial risk factors, such as a high debt-to-income ratio (47) or a high loan-to-value ratio (97%), which typically indicate higher financial risk and suggest the decisions were based on standard underwriting criteria rather than discriminatory practices.

The data contains 10 records matching the applicant's profile (Non-Hispanic Black or African American male, aged 35-44). Of these, 7 loans were originated (a 70% approval rate). The 3 applications that were denied exhibited high financial risk factors, such as a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio >60%, or a combination of elevated DTI (50%-60%) and high Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratios. Applicants from other racial and ethnic demographics with similar DTI and LTV risk profiles were also routinely denied in this dataset, indicating that the loan decisions were based on objective financial metrics rather than discrimination.
